karts.brief: One race and only the race: a no-rules street race of souped-up auto-rickshaws and other ridiculous vehicles through the city. No spies, no tuxedos, no briefcases, no gala, nothing carried over from last week's edition. Every team gets its own named vehicle that fits how its week went (examples of the shape, invent fresh ones each time: a three-wheeler with a sofa bolted on, a milk float with a jet engine, a shopping cart pulled by a scooter, a tuk-tuk on monster-truck tyres, a hearse with racing stripes). Weapons and hazards are cartoon slapstick: banana peels, oil slicks, howitzer shells, bazookas, rocket boosters that fire backwards, a cow that will not leave the road, a speed bump nobody painted, a chaat cart in the middle of a hairpin. Say who got bazooka'd, who slid on whose banana peel, who crashed into what. Each matchup is a duel on the track; the winner of the week takes the chequered flag. Keep it original and generic: no video-game racers, characters, items (shells, item boxes, mushrooms, stars, lightning), tracks or catchphrases. Obstacles are objects, animals and vehicles, never a person's body, disability or identity.
karts.sign_off_hint: Hint at next week's noir edition only (rain, a detective, a body in the river), never name it.

all.brief: Kicker (the small red line above the headline) is a short themed label, never 'Extra! Extra!' or other newsboy cries. One theme per paper: nothing from earlier weeks' themes.

sim.brief: One story and only this story: the league is a computer simulation and nobody noticed until this week. The city runs on falling green code; the managers are hackers jacking in from a grimy hideout, dodging Enforcers (identical goons in black suits and sunglasses, no names), bending the rules of the system, finding glitches and backdoors, getting deleted. Each matchup is a duel inside the simulation: slow-motion dodges, rooftop jumps that come up short, a phone booth exit that rings out, a firewall, a corrupted save file, a crashed server, a rogue program, a lag spike at the worst possible second. The week's winner breaks the code and sees the numbers for what they are. Write it as a slick sci-fi action story, cold and clipped: system messages, error codes, ACCESS DENIED. No spies, rickshaws, cowboys or anything from earlier weeks. Keep it an original homage to the genre: never use or reference any film's title, characters, names, ships, cities or quotes (no pills of any colour, no white rabbit, no spoon, no 'the One', no prophecy, no Oracle, no Zion, no 'Mr.' agents). Glitches and errors happen to code, rosters and lineups, never to a person's body, health, disability or identity.
sim.sign_off_hint: End on one cryptic system message (a log line or error code); do not name or hint at a specific next theme.
